newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Pacific 96 net seen lower-analysts.
newsitem.headline: First Pacific 96 net seen lower-analysts.

text.p: First Pacific Co Ltd is expected to announce a lower net profit for calendar 1996 on Monday due to the lack of huge exceptional gains, which contributed US$86.1 million to its 1995 profits, analysts said.
The Estimate Directory saw the consensus forecast at HK$1.55 billion (US$198.7 million), down 23 percent compared with 1995 net profit of HK$2.00 billion (US$257 million).

Vickers Ballas forecast the conglomerate to post a net of HK$1.66 billion (US$208 million) in 1996. "That represents a 22 percent growth in core earnings without exceptional items," Vickers research director Andrew Fernow said on Friday.

Morgan Stanley saw the company's 1996 net at HK$1.51 billion (US$194 million). Its regional conglomerate researcher Mike Warren said the earnings should be in line with market expectation since many of First Pacific's listed subsidiaries had published results.
"Looking down to the rest of their operation there is little room for a downside surprise and I don't think (the net profit) will be too far away from our number," he said.
A Japanese house analyst also expected First Pacific's operating profit to rise more than 20 percent in 1996 despite a sharp fall on yearly net.
"Its 1995 profit was greatly lifted by the exceptional item," he said.
The exceptional gain recored in 1995 was from dilution and disposal of shareholdings in subsidiaries and associated companies, First Pacific had said.
First Pacific mainly engages in marketing and distribution, telecommunications, property and banking.

Fernow said the major income of the company in 1996 was expected from the firm's global marketing and trading business which grew steadily and should account for more than 50 percent of the company's core earnings.
But intense competition in Hong Kong's telecommunication business had raised the market's conern on its local cellular telephone arms Pacific Link, analysts said.
This partly contributed to the shares' fall late to a low of HK$9.40 in December before the price gradually picked up from Janaury, they added.
One analyst said he believed that there will be no major profit growth for First Pacific's Hong Kong telecommunication business in the next few years.
"They are developing other telecommunication business around the region and is expected to offset the slow growth of Hong Kong," Fernow said.
He said the fall of First Pacific shares in late 1995 was also due to investor's shifted their interest to red chips or companies with a lot of China exposure.
Fernow saw share prices continue to pick up since the company has became more active in China and there would be some upcoming developments in the company for the month ahead, Fernow said.

The company was expected to announce to float of its Philippine cellular telephone arms, Smart Communications Co Inc, in June, and followed by some new developments in Philippines properties, he said.
Morgan's Mike Warren also said the major growth for the company in 1997 and 1998 was likely from the Philippines, Metro Pacific Corp, Hagemeyer NV and FPB Bank Holdings.
He estimated a 21 percent growth on First Pacific's net profit in 1997 to US$235 million.
Vicker's Fernow forecast the company's net profit to growth by 15 percent in 1997 plus a possible hefty exceptional gain from the expected float of Smart Communications.
Warren put a 12-month target for the company's share price on HK$15, compared with their Friday close of HK$10.85, down HK$0.15.
